anchor.quote: Let $f$ be the parameter of a call
Here $m$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
Let $s$ be the number of subcalls of one call.
Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.
Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$
Here $\Omega$ is the bit count of one axis chunk
Let $\nu$ count the levels of unrolling

anchor.note: sigma is introduced only by a range of allowed values; the page never says what it denotes (an auxiliary exponent for bounding the leaves).
big-O notation is covered by the profile
logarithms are covered by undergraduate discrete mathematics
summation and geometric series are covered by the calculus/discrete mathematics in the profile
maximum of two numbers is standard notation

gaps.quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
gaps.note: Only the cost of an interchange is cited; the page never says how a row addition is built from interchanges or why it costs this, nor why the call's outside work is a fixed number of row additions.

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk
gaps.note: A kernel is never defined or linked, so the reader cannot tell what handles a leaf or why it costs O(f/m^nu).
This contradicts the earlier s<Wm (so s/W<m) and the example s/W=3/2<m=2; the cited claim's content and role are not stated, and the reader cannot reconcile it with the condition used next.

gaps.quote: so the internal sum is at most a constant times $f^\lambda$ for every $\lambda>0$.
gaps.note: The ratio is below 1 only for lambda>log_m(s/W), so the claim for every lambda>0 contradicts the condition just stated; the reader cannot check it.
From d^theta <= f only f^sigma d^{theta(1-sigma)} <= f follows, not f^lambda; the page does not say why the d factor can be absorbed into f^{lambda-sigma}.
